strengths: Practical simplicity with minimal code changes (single line) and negligible computational overhead (0.4%), enabling broad adoption

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple dimensions: 5 model sizes (66M-2B), 2 architectures (dense and MoE), 2 datasets, 2 LR schedules, with statistical validation via multiple random seeds and robustness checks
Consistent improvements across all tested configurations (1-3% terminal loss reduction), particularly strong on MoE models and warmup-stable-decay schedules
Demonstrated orthogonality to other optimizers (Muon, Blockwise LR), suggesting complementary benefits with cumulative gains

Insightful empirical findings on noise-dependent behavior of optimal p with good alignment between theory (Example 5.1) and practice (p=1.2), plus novel observation of improved training stability for MoE models
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: sign-power transformations exist in prior Powerball work (Yuan et al., 2019); the distinction of studying both p<1 and p>1 regimes is incremental

Severe theory-practice gap: convergence analysis only covers Adagrad, not Adam where experiments are conducted; theoretical claims about 'amplifying flat directions' lack formal justification; whether LLM training is truly 'noise-dominated' remains empirically unverified

Incomplete hyperparameter guidance: while claiming p=1.2 is 'highly robust,' it was tuned on a single small-scale experiment; Figure 6 reveals non-trivial batch-size dependence but no principled selection strategy is provided for new domains

Limited experimental scope: maximum model size is 2B (10B+ needed for modern standards), sparse comparison with recent optimizers (missing Sophia, Apollo, AdamMini), and modest downstream task improvements (mixed results, ≤1% gains)

Loose theoretical-empirical connection: the 1D uniform-distribution toy example abstracts away high-dimensional complexities; claimed benefits for MoE models have limited theoretical justification and only one MoE architecture tested

Modest effect sizes with incomplete statistical reporting: main results (Figures 3-4) appear to be single runs without error bars despite showing stochasticity, and downstream task gains are inconsistent across benchmarks
